businessProblem: Go First has voluntarily filed for insolvency on 2 May 2023, citing faulty Pratt & Whitney engines grounding 50% of its A320neo fleet. It has exhausted all financial resources and owes ₹65.21 billion to financial creditors. Diagnose root causes and recommend highest-priority action plan.

evidence.finding: Go First owes financial creditors ₹65.21 billion (approximately USD 798 million) per NCLT filing as of 2 May 2023
Company stated it had 'exhausted all financial resources' in its NCLT voluntary insolvency filing
Revenue severely impaired by 50% capacity reduction due to fleet grounding
Approximately 25 aircraft — 50% of A320neo fleet — grounded due to Pratt & Whitney engine issues as of 1 May 2023
High fixed-cost airline model made the company extremely vulnerable to a 50% capacity shock
Active legal-commercial dispute with Pratt & Whitney over engine reliability and grounding — root cause not contractually resolved
Voluntary insolvency filing on 2 May 2023 — management acknowledged inability to continue without insolvency protection
Lessor and creditor claims likely to conflict during insolvency proceedings given complex aircraft-financing structures

ownerConstraintProfile.resistanceToChange: LOW — voluntary filing signals management acknowledges crisis
ownerConstraintProfile.managementCapability: LOW — cash exhausted, unable to resolve supplier dispute independently
ownerConstraintProfile.accountabilityWeakness: HIGH — cash exhausted without resolution plan
